bugs.error_message: OpenWolf install verification failed: expected OpenWolf runtime files are not ignored by git
bugs.root_cause: The verification script passed multiple paths to one `git check-ignore -q` invocation; that command exits non-zero if any supplied path is not ignored and did not identify paths individually, making the check brittle during repository bootstrap.
bugs.fix: Changed `checkGitIgnored()` to run `git check-ignore -q` once per expected runtime path and report the specific path that is not ignored.

bugs.error_message: Independent review found missing ignores for `.wolf/cerebrum-stats.json` and OpenWolf lock files, plus incomplete template hook verification.
bugs.root_cause: The initial bootstrap ignore/verification set covered common visible runtime files but missed generated cerebrum stats, transient lock artifacts from size-discipline writes, and full template/source JavaScript syntax coverage.
bugs.fix: Added ignore patterns for `.wolf/cerebrum-stats.json`, `.wolf/**/*.lock`, and `.wolf/**/*.lock.reclaim`; expanded `scripts/verify-install.js` to assert those ignores and syntax-check installed, source, and template hook/utility JavaScript files.

bugs.error_message: Second independent review found `scripts/verify-install.js` conflated a missing git repo with ignore-rule failures and did not assert scaffold files remain trackable.
bugs.root_cause: The git ignore verification treated all non-zero `git check-ignore` exits as ignore failures and only checked runtime files, leaving broad ignore patterns able to hide required scaffold files without detection.
bugs.fix: Added a `git rev-parse --is-inside-work-tree` preflight with a distinct failure message and added positive checks that representative scaffold files are not ignored by git.

bugs.error_message: Third independent review found scaffold trackability checks were still too narrow and `.wolf` log/state ignore globs were not recursive.
bugs.root_cause: The positive trackability assertions spot-checked only a small subset of required scaffold files, and `.wolf/*.log` / `.wolf/*-state.json` only matched one directory level.
bugs.fix: Expanded trackability assertions to include core `.claude`/`.wolf` scaffold files plus all installed/source/template hooks and utilities; added recursive `.wolf/**/*.log` and `.wolf/**/*-state.json` ignore patterns.

bugs.error_message: Fourth independent review found hook ESM package metadata was not verified and generated docs policy was ambiguous.
bugs.root_cause: The verifier omitted `.wolf/hooks/package.json` and `templates/wolf/hooks/package.json` from required JSON, ESM, and trackability checks; `.wolf/anatomy.md` and `.wolf/memory.md` were also not covered by an explicit tracked-vs-runtime policy.
bugs.fix: Added hook package manifests to required files, JSON parsing, `type=module` validation, and trackability checks; explicitly track-check `.wolf/anatomy.md` and `.wolf/memory.md` as intentional seed/self-hosting scaffold files.

bugs.error_message: Fifth independent review found named runtime JSON files were ignored only at top-level `.wolf/` paths, not recursively.
bugs.root_cause: Named runtime JSON ignore rules such as `.wolf/token-ledger.json` and `.wolf/cerebrum-stats.json` did not cover future nested runtime directories, and the verifier only probed top-level locations.
bugs.fix: Added recursive ignore variants for named runtime JSON files and added nested runtime probes for cerebrum stats, token ledger, and suggestions files in `scripts/verify-install.js`.

bugs.error_message: Sixth independent review found `templates/wolf/memory.md`, template trackability coverage, recursive QA markdown ignores, and runtime ignore probes were incomplete.
bugs.root_cause: The template source tree omitted a memory template, verifier trackability checks did not cover all required template files, `.wolf/qa/*.md` was non-recursive, and ignore probes sampled only part of the runtime file rules.
bugs.fix: Added `templates/wolf/memory.md`, added it to required files, expanded template trackability checks, added `.wolf/qa/**/*.md`, and expanded ignore probes for nested QA reductions and named runtime JSON files.

bugs.error_message: Independent review found daemon CPU/restart fixes still had PM2 autorestart, upgrade port-migration, PM2 action-targeting, dashboard exposure, and unsafe port-kill edge cases.
bugs.root_cause: The first daemon fix handled the primary spin/restart symptoms but left secondary lifecycle hazards: duplicate daemon exit code 0 could be autorestarted by PM2, migration logic treated a project-owned running daemon as an external port conflict, PM2 actions could target by colliding names instead of pm_id, dashboard listened on all interfaces, and stop/restart fallback could kill unrelated port owners.
bugs.fix: Started PM2 with --stop-exit-codes 0, guarded daemon start/restart and init port migration with project-root-aware PM2 ownership checks, used hash-qualified PM2 names and pm_id action targets, shell-quoted fallback names, preserved existing config on active upgrades, bound dashboard to 127.0.0.1, removed arbitrary PID-kill fallbacks, rebuilt dist, and iterated independent review to production-ready OK.

bugs.error_message: Independent review-0014 found remaining high-CPU/restart and portability flaws: reclaim-failed size locks could still loop, daemon singleton stale-lock handling could race or spin, and Windows hook imports used raw drive-letter paths.
bugs.root_cause: The previous fixes removed the obvious busy wait but left continue paths and daemon lock retry paths that could still loop under reclaim failure or partial lock files; hookCommand also did not convert Windows paths to file URLs for Node ESM imports.
bugs.fix: Changed acquireFileLock to return null when stale reclaim fails, made daemon singleton acquisition bounded with one atomic create/reclaim/create sequence and no unparseable-lock unlinking, converted hook dynamic imports through pathToFileURL, rebuilt dist, and iterated independent review to production-ready OK.

bugs.error_message: Independent review-0017 found existing PM2 daemons were not guaranteed to be migrated to --stop-exit-codes 0 and active legacy entries could be hidden by stale stopped hash entries.
bugs.root_cause: ensurePm2Daemon returned already-running for active hash entries and only applied stop-exit-codes on fresh starts; getOpenWolfPm2Process preferred hash entries even when stopped/errored while a same-root legacy daemon was active.
bugs.fix: Changed same-root legacy migration to delete/restart legacy entries under the hash-qualified name with --stop-exit-codes 0, added pm2 save after delete+start restart, and made PM2 lookup prefer an active legacy process over an inactive hash process. Rebuilt dist and independent review returned production-ready OK.

bugs.error_message: Independent review-0018 found dashboard bind/setup failures still exited 1, allowing PM2 to restart unrecoverable EADDRINUSE failures despite --stop-exit-codes 0.
bugs.root_cause: The server error handler released the singleton lock but exited with code 1, which remains restartable by PM2.
bugs.fix: Changed server error handler to release the singleton and exit 0 so PM2 stop-exit-codes suppresses restart loops for unrecoverable bind/setup failures. Rebuilt dist and got production-ready OK from independent review.

bugs.error_message: Independent review-0019 found active hash-qualified PM2 daemons started before the stop-exit-codes fix could remain already-running without migration, preserving restart-loop behavior.
bugs.root_cause: ensurePm2Daemon treated an active same-name PM2 daemon as already-running without checking whether PM2 stop_exit_codes included 0.
bugs.fix: Added hasStopExitCodeZero() and only return already-running for active same-name PM2 daemons that have stop_exit_codes containing 0; otherwise delete/restart with --stop-exit-codes 0 and pm2 save. Rebuilt dist and independent review returned production-ready OK.
